title: XML to JSON – Convert Sitemaps and RSS Feeds | OpenAnyDoc
description: Convert an XML file to JSON in your browser: attributes, text and repeated elements mapped clearly, then browse and download the .json.
heading: XML to JSON Converter
subtitle: Open or paste XML and it opens as JSON you can browse, search and download; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Turn an XML file, such as a sitemap, an RSS feed, a SOAP response or an export from an older system, into JSON you can work with. Open, drop or paste it and your browser's own XML parser reads it; the result opens in the JSON viewer as a tree and as text. Attributes become keys starting with @, element text goes under #text, repeated child elements become arrays, and an element that holds only text becomes a plain string. If the XML is malformed, the parser's message tells you the line to fix.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your XML is read by your own browser and never sent to a server, so nobody else sees it.

features.title: Clear mapping
features.text: @ for attributes, #text for text and arrays for repeated elements, the same rule everywhere in the file.

features.title: Works offline
features.text: Once this page has loaded, it keeps working without an internet connection.

stepsTitle: How it works: convert XML to JSON

steps.title: Open or paste your XML
steps.text: Choose an .xml file, drop it on the page, paste the text into the box, or try a sample.

steps.title: It opens as JSON
steps.text: The XML is parsed by the browser and shown in the JSON viewer. Malformed XML shows the parser's error with its line.

steps.title: Browse and download
steps.text: Expand the tree, search it, then download a .json file with the XML file's name.

handles: Text next to attributes or child elements is stored under "#text".
Repeated child elements with the same name become an array; a single child stays an object.
An element with only text, such as <title>Hello</title>, becomes the string "Hello".
Namespace prefixes stay in the names, such as "soap:Body" or "@xmlns:xsi".
Input from an .xml file, a drop, the paste box or a sample, up to 10 MB.
limits: No DTD or XSD validation: the file is checked for being well-formed, not against a schema.
Comments and processing instructions are dropped.
All values come out as strings; "42" in XML stays "42", because XML text has no types.
faqTitle: XML to JSON: questions and answers

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your XML is parsed by your browser's own XML parser, on your device. Pasted text stays in this tab and is never sent anywhere.

faq.question: Why do some keys start with @?
faq.answer: Those were attributes in the XML. The @ keeps them apart from child elements with the same name, so <item id="1"><id>9</id></item> gives both "@id" and "id".

faq.question: Why is one element an array and another an object?
faq.answer: A child element that appears more than once under its parent becomes an array; one that appears once stays a single value. If a list sometimes has one item, its JSON shape changes with it.

faq.question: My XML will not open. What is wrong?
faq.answer: It is not well-formed: a tag is not closed, an & is not escaped, or there are two top elements. The page shows the parser's message with the line number, so you can fix it in the file and open it again.

faq.question: Is the XML checked against my XSD schema?
faq.answer: No. Only well-formedness is checked; DTD and XSD validation are not done. Use a schema validator if the structure has to match a contract.

faq.question: Can I convert JSON back to XML?
faq.answer: Yes, on the JSON to XML page. The two pages follow different rules, so a round trip may not give the same file.

faq.question: How do I convert XML to JSON?
faq.answer: Convert XML to JSON by turning elements into keys, attributes into keys that start with @ and repeated elements into arrays. In OpenAnyDoc, open, drop or paste the XML and the JSON opens in the JSON viewer as a tree and as text, ready to download; the XML is read in your browser and never uploaded.
